gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the only like-for-like charging-noise pair is from one reviewer, The Technology Man. Using the same 1 m distance, room temperature and full-speed charging on UK mains, they measured about 37 dB for the DJI Power 1000 V2 (over 1,400 W) and about 42 dB for the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (1,600 W). Notebookcheck measured the same Anker at 45 dB at 1 m. Every quiet-mode dB figure on the maker pages either names a different distance and charge rate or names none at all, so those figures cannot be ranked against each other.
standout_why: I compared against thepowerstationguide.com, voltandvalley.com and powerstationgeek.com. thepowerstationguide.com already lists DJI Power 1000 at about 23 dB (1 m, 25°C, 600 W recharge) next to Jackery's 22 dB with no stated conditions and Anker's 20 dB on discharge. It also explains the 6 dB drop for each doubling of distance and warns not to normalise figures that give no distance. That covers half of this angle. voltandvalley.com says Jackery's 22 dB has no distance or wattage and gives no figures for DJI, BLUETTI or EcoFlow. powerstationgeek.com gives 41 dB for the DELTA 3 Plus and 59 dB for the original C1000, but states no distance and whether the unit was charging. None of the three says that the DJI 37 dB and Anker 42 dB come from the same reviewer under the same method. None gives Notebookcheck's 45 dB for the C1000 Gen 2. None says that the 23 dB figure DJI publishes is for the original Power 1000, not the V2. None says that PCWorld's AC180 dB figures were taken while the unit was powering a load, not charging.
decides: This confirms the DJI Power 1000 V2 as the quiet choice for full-speed charging. Under one reviewer's identical setup it was about 5 dB quieter than the Anker C1000 Gen 2 while charging faster than 1,400 W. A second reviewer, Notebookcheck, put the Anker even louder at 45 dB at 1 m. For overnight charging the pick does not change. The Anker's fans switch off at 200 W, which The Technology Man observed directly. By contrast, Jackery's 22 or 30 dB claim and DJI's quiet-mode claim are maker numbers taken under different or unstated conditions, so neither can be ranked against the other.

findings.label: Measured noise while AC charging at full speed
findings.source_title: This compact power station can output 2600W – DJI Power 1000 V2 review (The Technology Man)
findings.note: Fast mode on UK mains with the supplied lead, charging 'at over 1400W'. Ambient was about 21°C and the dB meter model is not named. The reviewer describes it as barely above background noise. Standard (about 600 W) mode was not measured. Full charge took under 53 minutes.

findings.label: Measured noise while AC charging at full speed (same reviewer and method as the DJI figure)
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review (The Technology Man)
findings.note: UltraFast mode at 1,600 W, ambient about 20°C, full charge in 47 minutes. The reviewer notes that the varying fan speed makes the noise more noticeable. Compared with the DJI V2 figure from the same reviewer, the Anker is about 5 dB louder at the same distance.

findings.label: Fan behaviour at the reduced charge rates
findings.value: fans off at 200 W; 600 W ('Silent' in Anker's app) is 'a lot quieter but not silent'
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review (The Technology Man)
findings.note: The reviewer gives no dB figure at 200 W or 600 W. Charge speed can be set in 100 W steps, down to 100 W. Our arithmetic: 1,024 Wh ÷ 200 W is about 5.1 h before charging losses, and 1,024 Wh ÷ 600 W is about 1.7 h.

findings.label: Second reviewer's measured noise during fast AC charging
findings.source_title: Lighter, stronger and faster, but...: Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 power station review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Measured 'at higher power output and fast AC charging'. Notebookcheck measured about 1,200 W of charging power near the end of a charge that took just under 55 minutes without Boost. That is 3 dB above The Technology Man's 42 dB for the same unit, which shows how much single-reviewer figures can vary.

findings.label: DJI's own noise figure and the conditions it states
findings.value: about 23 dB at 100 cm, 25°C, 600 W Standard Recharge Mode
findings.source_title: DJI Power 1000 – Online Customer Service (DJI support)
findings.note: This is the only maker claim I opened that states distance, temperature and charge rate. It is for the original Power 1000. thepowerstationguide.com lists it as 'DJI Power 1000', and the page gives no figure for the V2. Do not carry it over to the V2.

findings.label: Conditions stated for Jackery's quiet-charging claim
findings.value: below 22 dB, with no distance, charge wattage or method given
findings.source_title: Are Portable Power Stations Loud? Only Two Publish a Figure (Volt & Valley)
findings.note: Volt & Valley has not measured it and says a unit charging at 1,000 W 'is not going to be at 22dB'. thepowerstationguide.com also lists '≤22 dB, quiet charging' with no distance. Because no distance is stated, this cannot be put on the same 1 m basis as the DJI figures.

findings.label: PCWorld's dB readings are output-load figures, not charging figures
findings.value: 40 dBA at a 200 W load, 43–44 dBA at 800 W, about 45 dBA at 1,500 W, measured at 3 ft facing a fan; fans do not start below about 100 W
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 power station review: Super efficient, super value (PCWorld)
findings.note: These were taken while the unit was powering loads, so they should not go in a charging-noise column. PCWorld gives no Silent or Turbo charging measurement. The AC inlet is rated at 1,440 W.

findings.label: How to normalise across distances
findings.value: about −6 dB for each doubling of distance in free field, only approximate indoors; figures with no stated distance should not be normalised
findings.source_title: Portable Power Station Noise Levels: What to Expect (2026) | The Power Station Guide
findings.note: A rival page ChatGPT cited already says this. It also lists EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus at ≤25 dB at 0.5 m, 600 W, 25°C. That model is 2,048 Wh, outside this class. By the 6 dB rule it would be roughly 19 dB at 1 m, which is our arithmetic and only indicative.
